easy.prompt: Which statement best defines unsupervised learning?
options: It predicts a known target from labelled examples.
It always learns through rewards and penalties.
It requires a correct class label for every record.
It discovers patterns or structure in data without supplied target labels.

easy.prompt: What is a label in machine learning?
options: The known target answer attached to a record.
A principal component created by PCA.
A random identifier added after clustering.

easy.prompt: Which dataset is most clearly unlabelled?
options: Customer records containing age, income and spending, but no target category.
Houses with features and known sale prices.
Emails marked spam or not spam.

easy.prompt: What is the main goal of clustering?
options: Assign a known class to each observation.
Reduce every dataset to exactly two features.
Group observations so members of the same cluster are relatively similar.

easy.prompt: In clustering, strong cohesion means that:
options: points within the same cluster are close or similar.
all clusters contain exactly the same number of points.
the model uses labelled target values.

easy.prompt: Which description best matches the pattern shown in Figure 1?
options: Three compact clusters, each represented by a centroid.
A single cluster with no internal structure.

easy.prompt: In K-means, what does K represent?
options: The number of labelled classes in a test set.
The number of anomalies to delete.
The number of clusters to create.

easy.prompt: What does a K-means centroid represent?
options: The most distant observation in a cluster.
A class label supplied by a teacher.
The mean position of the observations assigned to a cluster.

easy.prompt: Why is feature scaling often important before K-means?
options: Scaling converts K-means into supervised learning.
Large-scale features can otherwise dominate distance calculations.
Scaling automatically selects the best K.
K-means can only process integer values.

easy.prompt: The Elbow Method is mainly used to:
options: estimate a suitable number of clusters for K-means.
identify the exact number of anomalies in all datasets.

easy.prompt: On a standard Elbow Method graph, the y-axis usually shows:
options: the number of principal components only.

easy.prompt: What is the range of the silhouette coefficient?
A silhouette value close to +1 usually indicates:
options: a well-matched point that is well separated from neighbouring clusters.
the point must be an anomaly.
a point is probably assigned to the wrong cluster.

easy.prompt: Hierarchical clustering is called hierarchical because it:
options: sorts features from largest to smallest.
builds nested grouping relationships that can be represented as a tree.
requires labels arranged in a hierarchy.

easy.prompt: What is a dendrogram?
options: A chart of WCSS against K.
A tree-like diagram showing how observations or clusters merge or split.
A plot of support against confidence only.

easy.prompt: DBSCAN is best described as a:
Which two parameters are central to DBSCAN?
In common DBSCAN implementations, the label -1 represents:
Which method is a probabilistic soft-clustering model?
In a GMM, a responsibility is best understood as:
options: the probability-like degree to which a component explains an observation.

easy.prompt: What is the main purpose of dimensionality reduction?
options: Increase every dataset to more features.
Represent data using fewer dimensions while retaining useful information or structure.
Create target labels for unlabelled data.

easy.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes feature selection from feature extraction?
options: Feature selection keeps original variables; feature extraction creates new transformed variables.

easy.prompt: PCA is primarily a:
options: linear dimensionality-reduction technique based on directions of high variance.

easy.prompt: What does PCA create?
options: Principal components that are new directions formed from the original features.

easy.prompt: t-SNE is mainly used to:
options: visualize high-dimensional data in two or three dimensions.

easy.prompt: What kind of structure does t-SNE emphasize most strongly?
options: Exact global distances between all groups.

easy.prompt: Association-rule learning is commonly used for:
options: finding items or events that frequently occur together.

easy.prompt: Which measure tells how frequently an itemset occurs in the full transaction dataset?
Anomaly detection aims to identify:
options: observations or patterns that differ substantially from normal behaviour.

easy.prompt: Customer segmentation with K-means is an unsupervised task mainly because:
options: the customer groups are discovered from features rather than supplied as target labels.
all customers already have correct segment labels.
K-means predicts a continuous sales target.
the data contains no numerical features.

medium.prompt: A retailer has numerical variables measured in rupees, visits per month and years. What is the best preparation before distance-based clustering?
options: Convert every value into a target label.
Remove all variables except the largest-scale one.
Standardize or otherwise scale the features to comparable ranges.

medium.prompt: Why can choosing K that is too small be harmful in K-means?
options: Every observation becomes its own cluster.
Distinct natural groups may be merged into overly broad clusters.

medium.prompt: Using Figure 2, which K is the strongest elbow candidate?
Why is the lowest possible WCSS not automatically the best K-means solution?
options: WCSS always decreases as K increases and can be made trivial with too many clusters.
WCSS cannot be computed for numerical data.
WCSS becomes negative for good clusters.

medium.prompt: Using Figure 3, which candidate K has the best average silhouette score?
For a point i, a(i)=1.2 and b(i)=4.8. What is its silhouette coefficient?
What does a negative silhouette value most strongly suggest for an observation?
options: It may be closer to another cluster than to its assigned cluster.
It is perfectly centered in its assigned cluster.
The dataset contains only one feature.

medium.prompt: Which linkage method uses the minimum pairwise distance between two clusters?
Which linkage method chooses the merge causing the smallest increase in within-cluster variance?
If a horizontal line is drawn across a dendrogram, how is the number of clusters commonly estimated?
options: Count the leaves below the first merge only.
Count the vertical branches intersected by the cut.

medium.prompt: A DBSCAN point has at least MinPts observations in its eps-neighbourhood. It is therefore a:
What usually happens if eps is set far too small in DBSCAN?
options: Many observations fail to connect and are labelled as noise or tiny fragments.
The number of principal components increases.

medium.prompt: Which dataset characteristic is a notable strength of DBSCAN?
options: Clusters can have irregular, non-spherical shapes and include noise.
Every cluster must be spherical and equally sized.
All observations must have class labels.
The correct K must be supplied in advance.

medium.prompt: What is the purpose of a k-distance graph in DBSCAN tuning?
options: To identify a knee that can suggest a useful eps value.

medium.prompt: In a GMM, which parameter describes the relative prevalence of a component in the mixture?
What occurs in the E-step of the EM algorithm for a GMM?
options: A dendrogram is cut into clusters.
All covariance matrices are set to zero.
Responsibilities of components for observations are estimated using current parameters.

medium.prompt: What occurs in the M-step of EM for a GMM?
options: Component parameters are updated using the current responsibilities.
Labels are supplied by a human.

medium.prompt: Why might GMM be preferred over K-means for some data?
options: It always finds arbitrary shapes better than DBSCAN.
It can model overlapping clusters with probabilistic membership and flexible covariance shapes.

medium.prompt: Why should numerical features often be standardized before PCA?
options: It guarantees every component explains equal variance.
Features with larger measurement scales can otherwise dominate the variance.

medium.prompt: If PC1 explains 52% and PC2 explains 28% of variance, how much variance do the first two components explain together?
Using Figure 4, what is the minimum number of components needed to retain at least 80% explained variance?
Which statement about PCA loadings is most accurate?
options: They describe how strongly original variables contribute to principal components.
They are target labels assigned by supervisors.

medium.prompt: Which t-SNE parameter roughly controls the scale of local neighbourhoods considered by the method?
Why should a t-SNE map not be interpreted as proof that visible groups are true clusters?
options: t-SNE uses known labels to draw groups.
A t-SNE plot always preserves exact global distances.
t-SNE emphasizes local structure and the global layout can change with settings and random initialization.

medium.prompt: What does confidence(X → Y) measure?
options: The difference between two cluster centroids.
The proportion of transactions containing X that also contain Y.
How often Y appears in the full dataset regardless of X.

medium.prompt: A rule has lift greater than 1. What does this indicate?
options: X and Y co-occur more often than expected under independence.

medium.prompt: Why is Apriori able to prune many candidate itemsets?
options: Any subset of a frequent itemset must itself be frequent.

medium.prompt: Which algorithm is often preferred over Apriori on large dense transaction data because it avoids explicit candidate generation?
Which example is a contextual anomaly rather than simply an isolated value?
options: A temperature that is normal in summer but highly unusual for the same location in winter.
A group of normal transactions with no unusual pattern.
A centroid near the center of its cluster.
A single extremely large sensor value regardless of context.

medium.prompt: In a customer-segmentation workflow, why should cluster profiles be interpreted after fitting K-means?
options: Numeric cluster IDs have no business meaning until their feature patterns are examined and named.
Clusters must be converted into target labels before analysis.
Interpretation is unnecessary when WCSS is low.

hard.prompt: Five transactions are: T1 Bread/Milk/Butter; T2 Bread/Milk/Eggs; T3 Bread/Butter/Diapers; T4 Milk/Butter/Diapers; T5 Bread/Milk/Butter/Eggs/Diapers. What is Support(Bread → Butter)?
Using the same five-transaction dataset, what is Confidence(Bread → Butter)?
Using the same dataset, Support(Butter)=0.80 and Confidence(Bread → Butter)=0.75. What is the lift?
Figure 5 compares rule lift values. Which rule provides evidence of a positive association?
A rule has 90% confidence but lift = 0.85. What is the best interpretation?
options: The rule proves a strong positive causal effect.
The rule is guaranteed to generalize.
The rule must have zero support.
The consequent is common, and the antecedent does not increase its occurrence above baseline.

hard.prompt: Why can X → Y and Y → X have the same support but different confidence?
options: Support depends on co-occurrence, while confidence divides by the support of the antecedent, which changes with direction.

hard.prompt: In K-means, two points (2,4) and (6,8) are assigned to the same cluster. If they are the only points in that cluster, what is the updated centroid?
A K-means model produces WCSS values 700, 390, 205, 172 and 158 for K=1..5. Which K is most defensible by the Elbow Method?
options: K = 5 because it has the smallest WCSS.
K = 3 because improvements become much smaller after that point.
K = 2 because WCSS first decreases there.

hard.prompt: Why should the Elbow Method and silhouette score be combined with domain interpretation?
options: Silhouette and WCSS are supervised metrics.
Both metrics directly provide business names for clusters.
A mathematically attractive partition may still be unstable, meaningless or unusable in the real problem.

hard.prompt: For point P, a(P)=3.0 and b(P)=2.0. What is s(P) and what does it imply?
options: -1/3 ≈ -0.33; P may fit a neighbouring cluster better.

hard.prompt: A clustering solution has a high average silhouette score, but one cluster contains many negative individual silhouette values. What should the analyst do?
options: Replace the silhouette score with supervised accuracy.
Accept the solution automatically because the average is high.
Delete all negative-valued observations without review.
Inspect that cluster because the average can hide local misassignment or overlap.

hard.prompt: Using Figure 6, how many clusters are obtained by cutting the dendrogram at height 3.5?
In the Figure 6 dendrogram, why do the left and right large groups remain separate at the 3.5 cut?
options: A dendrogram cut always creates exactly two groups.
They contain different numbers of leaves.
Their final merge occurs above the cut height.

hard.prompt: Which linkage method is most susceptible to a chaining effect where clusters grow through sequences of nearby points?
Why can complete linkage produce more compact clusters than single linkage?
options: It evaluates the farthest pair of points when deciding how close two clusters are.
It uses only the nearest pair.

hard.prompt: A dataset contains two crescent-shaped dense groups plus isolated points, as in Figure 7. Which algorithm is most naturally suited?
For DBSCAN with MinPts=5, a point has exactly five observations in its eps-neighbourhood when counting itself. How is it classified with respect to density?
options: It qualifies as a core point.
It is automatically a border point.

hard.prompt: What is the likely effect of making eps too large in DBSCAN?
options: Separate dense regions may merge into one broad cluster.
Every point becomes a principal component.

hard.prompt: Why can one global eps value be problematic when a dataset contains clusters with very different densities?
options: eps controls the number of PCA components.
An eps suitable for a sparse cluster may merge dense clusters, while one suited to dense clusters may fragment sparse ones.

hard.prompt: A k-distance curve remains flat and then rises sharply near distance 0.42. What is a reasonable initial DBSCAN tuning decision?
options: Set eps to the largest observed distance.
Test eps values around the knee near 0.42 and validate the resulting clusters.

hard.prompt: A GMM gives an observation responsibilities [0.10, 0.75, 0.15] for components 1-3. What is the hard assignment if one is required?
options: No component because responsibilities must be equal.

hard.prompt: Which GMM feature allows clusters to be elongated or differently oriented rather than strictly spherical?
Why can GMM assign meaningful membership to an observation near the overlap of two clusters?
options: It uses labelled class probabilities from training targets.
It estimates probabilities/responsibilities for multiple components instead of only a hard nearest-centroid label.
It removes all overlapping points as noise.

hard.prompt: When comparing GMMs with different numbers of components using BIC, which choice is generally preferred?
options: Always the model with the most components.
The model with the highest BIC.
Always the model with one component.
The model with the lower BIC, balancing fit against model complexity.

hard.prompt: In EM for a GMM, why are E-steps and M-steps repeated?
options: Each repetition increases the number of features.
Responsibilities and component parameters depend on each other, so they are iteratively refined until convergence.
EM must create target labels manually.
The algorithm alternates between PCA and DBSCAN.

hard.prompt: A PCA model has eigenvalues 5, 3, 1 and 1. What percentage of total variance is explained by PC1?
With eigenvalues 5, 3, 1 and 1, how much cumulative variance is explained by the first two PCs?
If two original variables are strongly positively correlated, why can PCA often reduce dimensionality effectively?
options: Correlation forces all eigenvalues to be equal.
PCA duplicates correlated variables into more dimensions.
Much of their shared variation can be represented along a smaller number of principal directions.
PCA converts the variables into target labels.

hard.prompt: Why are PCA principal components mutually orthogonal in the standard formulation?
options: They are constructed as perpendicular directions capturing successive, non-redundant variance.
DBSCAN forces them to be perpendicular.
They correspond to independent target classes.

hard.prompt: A pipeline scales data and fits PCA before the train-test split. What is the key methodological problem?
options: The number of components must equal the number of rows.
PCA can only be fitted after K-means.
Information from the future test set leaks into the fitted preprocessing transformation.

hard.prompt: Figure 4 shows PC1=52%, PC2=28%, PC3=12%, PC4=5%, PC5=3%. If the retention target is at least 90%, what is the minimum number of PCs?
Why might PCA be a poor choice when the most important structure is strongly nonlinear?
options: PCA always keeps every original feature unchanged.
PCA only finds linear projection directions and may miss curved manifold structure.

hard.prompt: Which claim about the visible spacing between groups in Figure 8 is safest?
options: The plot guarantees K=4 is the optimal clustering solution.
The four groups are proven ground-truth classes.
Nearby points within a group may indicate local similarity, but large between-group distances should not be treated as exact global distances.
The exact distance between group 1 and group 4 is preserved from the original space.

hard.prompt: Why does t-SNE use a heavy-tailed Student t-distribution in the low-dimensional space?
options: It guarantees exact preservation of all global distances.
It helps reduce the crowding problem and allows moderately distant points to remain separated.

hard.prompt: What objective does t-SNE iteratively minimize?
options: Kullback-Leibler divergence between high- and low-dimensional similarity distributions.

hard.prompt: Two t-SNE runs with different random seeds produce rotated or rearranged global layouts but similar local neighbourhoods. What is the best conclusion?
options: The stable local relationships are more trustworthy than the exact global arrangement.
The method has discovered supervised labels.
One run must be mathematically invalid.
The data cannot contain any structure.

hard.prompt: An anomaly detector threshold is lowered substantially. What trade-off is most likely?
options: Fewer observations are flagged and false negatives always increase.
More observations are flagged, increasing sensitivity but often also false positives.

hard.prompt: Which situation best illustrates a collective anomaly?
options: A sequence of individually ordinary network events that becomes suspicious because of their unusual combined pattern.
A cluster centroid at the mean.

hard.prompt: Why is evaluating unsupervised anomaly detection difficult when ground-truth labels are unavailable?
options: There may be no definitive reference showing which flagged observations are truly abnormal.
All anomalies must have negative silhouette scores.
Anomaly scores cannot be calculated without labels.
Unsupervised models cannot output any alerts.

hard.prompt: A customer-segmentation solution has the best silhouette at K=5, but K=4 is slightly lower and produces four stable, actionable business segments while K=5 splits one segment without a useful distinction. Which decision is strongest?
options: Always choose K=5 because the silhouette score is mathematically highest.
Prefer K=4 if stability and business usefulness outweigh the small metric difference.
Use a supervised accuracy score instead.
